findings.description: The reports bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so objects (including the uploaded vendor roster) are stored without enforced SSE-KMS/SSE-S3 encryption.

No acl is set and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or bucket policy restricts public access, leaving the bucket's exposure dependent on account defaults and allowing accidental public ACLs/policies.
The bucket has no logging block, so read/write access to the stored data cannot be audited or attributed during an incident.
Versioning is not enabled, so objects deleted or overwritten by an attacker (or ransomware) cannot be recovered and tampering is undetectable.
force_destroy = true allows the bucket and all its contents to be deleted without emptying it first, enabling irrecoverable data destruction via a Terraform run.
The ledger export bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so sensitive financial exports are stored without enforced encryption at rest.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is attached, so a future bucket policy or object ACL could expose ledger data publicly despite the private canned ACL.
No logging block is configured for this bucket, so access to ledger exports is not recorded for audit or forensic purposes.
Versioning is not enabled on the ledger bucket, so malicious overwrites or deletions of financial records are unrecoverable.
force_destroy = true permits deletion of the bucket along with all ledger objects, increasing the blast radius of a compromised pipeline credential.
The model artifacts bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving stored artifacts unencrypted at rest by default.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource restricts public ACLs or policies on this bucket, so it can be made public unintentionally.
force_destroy = true allows the bucket and all versioned model artifacts to be destroyed in a single operation.
The runbooks bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration; runbooks often contain operational and credential-adjacent details and are stored unencrypted at rest.
No logging block is configured, so reads of operational runbooks cannot be audited.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block guards this bucket against public ACLs or policies.
force_destroy = true allows the bucket and its contents to be deleted without being emptied first.
The audit/log-delivery bucket itself has no logging configuration and no public access block, so access to the central audit logs is neither recorded nor protected from accidental public exposure.
force_destroy = true on the audit trail bucket allows all security log data to be deleted in one operation, undermining log integrity and non-repudiation.

The vendor roster spreadsheet is uploaded with no kms_key_id or server_side_encryption argument into a bucket that also lacks default encryption, so this potentially sensitive data is stored in plaintext.
